CLASS 32 · PRESCHOOL AGES 4–5

Life Skills & Good Habits

Age 4–5 YearsClass 32Activities 29 live of 30Subjects Hygiene · manners · independence

The everyday skills grown-ups use without thinking — washing hands, tidying up, kind words, asking for help — learned the way four-year-olds learn best: on real activity sheets, doing the circle, the match, the trace and the draw all by themselves.

Every activity opens right here on the site: the sheet sits on the left and your child writes, circles, traces and draws straight on top of it. The instructions sit beside them in grown-up read-aloud words. Their finished work saves as a real picture they can keep.

Start the first activity →One or two sheets per sitting is a full class.

SUPPORTING RESOURCE · EXPLORE LIFE SKILLS FLASHCARDS

Explore the Life Skills Flashcards.

The activities on this page teach HOW to do each skill, step by step, right on the screen. FOR GROWN-UPS

Every sheet follows five friendly steps.

The sheets keep one shape on purpose: after the first sheet your child already knows how to play the next one. The same five moves, new good habits.

  1. 1

    Circle it

    One right picture to circle — looking closely is the whole game.

  2. 2

    Match them

    Draw lines from the left side to the right side.

  3. 3

    Choose one

    Two choices — tick or circle the one that fits.

  4. 4

    Trace it

    Big tracing words, any color you like.

  5. 5

    Draw it

    The last box is all yours — draw!

Nothing is scored and nothing is timed. A sheet your child saved is a sheet finished — the “Cleared!” ribbon is theirs to keep, saved separately for each child you set up in My Classroom.

A NOTE FROM THE PRINCIPAL

For the grown-ups.

Life skills are not learned from a poster — they are practised on real days, with real hands. These sheets give the practice a picture: your child circles the child washing hands, and somewhere that evening they will wash theirs with a little more purpose. Keep the words big, the praise specific and the sessions short. The drawing layer is a real pencil as far as a four-year-old is concerned, and saving their finished sheet — their own circles and squiggles over the real artwork — is the proudest ending there is.

NEXT ON THE PATH

Next: Feelings & Kindness (Class 38).

The habits this class practises — gentle hands, kind words, taking turns, deep breaths — meet their feelings words next door: Class 38 teaches the same skills with a vocabulary, thirty-five cards from happy, sad, angry and calm to the kindness graduation. It sits at the end of the path by design — the habits shelf grew a feelings shelf, and Class 32 points to it as the natural next step.

GOOD MANNERS NEXT

Practise good manners.

Class 32 builds the habits; the school’s Manners flashcards drill them one card at a time: thirty-two printable manners for ages 3–5 — waiting turns, gentle hands, quiet voices, table manners — each with a one-line practice tip, a download button and one-tap printing, all on a single page. Habits here, manners next door: the two decks finish each other.

ROUTINES, PICTURED

The habits, four steps at a time.

Class 32 builds the daily habits; the Sequence Stories flashcards tell them as little stories: wash-your-hands, tidy-the-toys, set-the-table and put-on-your-coat are all in the deck — twenty-four printable four-picture sequences for ages 3–5, each with a practice tip, a download button and one-tap printing on a single page. Two of the kitchen cards even carry an Ask a grown-up badge, because hot jobs belong to grown-ups.

THE SAFETY CLASS NEXT DOOR

Staying Safe: the rules that guard the habits.

Class 32 builds the habits a good day runs on; Class 39 · Staying Safe guards the body those habits live in: nineteen printable cards for ages 4–5 — buckle up, hot things, medicine is not candy, stop-look-listen, the stop-drop-roll drill — all on one page, the rule quoted from the card and one way to practise it today. Habits here, safety next door: rehearse a rule a week and the whole set sticks.

HABITS AT THE TABLE

Class 40 · Healthy Food & Eating Well.

Class 32 builds the daily habits — hand-washing, helping, asking for help — and the Healthy Food & Eating Well class grows the same skills at the table: twenty-one printable food cards for ages 4–5, from wash-your-hands and sit-down to try-new-foods and feel-full, each right here with one tiny thing to try tonight. Same habit method, happier plates.

HABITS ON THE CLOCK

Class 41 · Time & Daily Routine.

Class 32 builds the daily habits — hand-washing, tidying, getting ready — and the Time & Daily Routine class puts those habits on the clock: forty-one printable time cards for ages 4–5, from the five morning steps and the same-time-each-day routine to work time and break time — every card downloads and prints straight from the class page, with the rule and one way to try it today right under the picture. Same habit method — now with the time words that make the day hold together.

GOOD HABITS START WITH GOOD PEOPLE

Class 45 · Family & Friends.

Class 32 practises the habits — hand-washing, tidying up, kind words — and the Family & Friends class names the people we practise them with. Thirty-five printable family and friends flashcards for ages 4–5, every card on the one class page, each with a try-it-today job: set the table for Dad, draw Auntie a picture, wave hello to a neighbor.

THE HABITS HAVE VERBS

Class 49 · Action Words.

Class 32 builds the habits a good day runs on; Class 49 · Action Words names the verbs those habits are made of: twenty-four printable action-word flashcards for ages 4–5 — clean, sweep, dry, fix, pack, wash, tie, wait your turn — every card showing the action as a kid does it, right here with one way to try it today. The habit names the what; the verb names the how.

Prefer printed cards?

Wash Your Hands

Clean hands before eating, a toothbrush for every child and a breakfast that is really healthy.

THE ACTIVITY — WRITE AND DRAW RIGHT ON THE SHEET

Your sheet is ready.

Pick a color or the eraser, then circle, match, trace and draw straight on the sheet with your finger, a stylus or the mouse. Press Save my work when you are proud — that is what marks this activity cleared for your child.

Drawing on the sheet needs JavaScript. The printable twin at /worksheets/life-skills/wash-your-hands/ always works.

FOR GROWN-UPS

What this sheet practises.

Ask “when do we wash our hands?” during the day — before eating, after the toilet, after playing outside. The sheet names the habit; the day reinforces it.

  • Hand-washing before eating
  • Toothbrush ownership
  • Healthy food choices
  • Word tracing
  • Habit awareness

See how hand washing fits into a doctor visit: the Doctor Visit class walks the whole check-up card by card — and its hand-washing card ends the visit the way this sheet starts the day. Clean hands, both times.
